newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK poll shows faith in future leader Tung slips.
newsitem.headline: HK poll shows faith in future leader Tung slips.

text.p: Most people are confident about Hong Kong's political and economic future as its return to China draws closer, but faith in their future leader Tung Chee-hwa seems to be slipping, opinion polls showed on Monday.

A poll commissioned by the English-language South China Morning Post said 57 percent of respondents expected Hong Kong to be as prosperous in the future as it was now, while 25 percent thought it would become even more prosperous.

Up to 51 percent expected the British colony of more than 150 years to remain stable after it is handed back to China at midnight on June 30, while 34 percent felt that stability would suffer, the poll showed.
The survey quizzed 1,075 respondents between April 7 and 11.
A separate poll commissioned by the Chinese-language Apple Daily indicated the public's rating of former shipping tycoon Tung, who will lead Hong Kong from July 1, has slipped.
In a survey of 692 people conducted on April 24 and 25 by the Chinese University of Hong Kong, Tung's overall popularity fell to 60.4 percent, from 62.6 percent in a March 20 poll.
The drop occurred after Tung announced plans to curb protests and ban foreign funding of local political groups after the handover.
Respondents' feelings of trust in Tung fell to a new low of 56.8 percent from 62.8 percent, the Apple Daily poll showed.
The number of people who believe he will protect Hong Kong's freedoms after the handover dropped to 50.3 percent from 54.8 percent in the previous poll.
